title: Cloudflare BGP policy rollout outage
alert: Cloudflare reported connectivity failures at some major edge locations during a routing configuration rollout. Determine the affected footprint, cause and documented recovery approach.

evidence.text: Routing configuration reached busiest locations before the MCP-enabled sites were affected.
Deployment at MCP-enabled sites took 19 locations offline; these facilities handled about half of global requests.
Engineers made an initial router change to test the failure mechanism.
Engineers identified the routing policy problem and began rolling back the bad change; first site was restored.
The last affected data center was brought online after reverts were completed.
A misordered BGP policy rejected site-local announcements, disrupting internal reachability and load balancing.
evidence.source_section: Technical description of the error and how it happened

evidence.text: The staged deployment process failed to include an MCP-enabled site until the final step.

impact_options.name: Approximately 50% of traffic handled by those sites

root_hypotheses.description: A BGP route policy change withdrew/rejected critical site-local prefixes in MCP data centers
A malicious DNS hijack of global authoritative nameservers
An upstream utility blackout across all data centers

response_options.description: Revert the faulty routing policy at affected routers and verify site restoration
Wait for hardware replacement before changing routing

dataset_origin: Published first-party incident postmortem; curated and paraphrased source facts (NOT original telemetry)
